examples.title: List namespaces
examples.description: List one page of active namespaces. Follow pagination.nextOffset while it is nonzero to retrieve further pages.

snippets.code:
from opentdf_tdf3.protocol.policy.namespaces import namespaces_pb2
from opentdf_tdf3.protocol.policy import selectors_pb2

request = namespaces_pb2.ListNamespacesRequest(
    pagination=selectors_pb2.PageRequest(limit=25, offset=0),
)
response = await client.namespaces.list_namespaces_async(request)
print(response)

examples.title: Create a namespace
examples.description: Create a policy namespace with an administrative identity. The example response illustrates a server-assigned ID; retain the actual returned ID for later requests.

snippets.code:
from opentdf_tdf3.protocol.policy.namespaces import namespaces_pb2

request = namespaces_pb2.CreateNamespaceRequest(
    name="example.com",
)
response = await client.namespaces.create_namespace_async(request)
print(response)

examples.title: List attributes in a namespace
examples.description: List one page of attributes in an existing namespace. Replace example.com with your namespace name or ID.

snippets.code:
from opentdf_tdf3.protocol.policy.attributes import attributes_pb2
from opentdf_tdf3.protocol.policy import selectors_pb2

request = attributes_pb2.ListAttributesRequest(
    namespace="example.com",
    pagination=selectors_pb2.PageRequest(limit=25, offset=0),
)
response = await client.attributes.list_attributes_async(request)
print(response)

import OpenTDFTDF3

var request = Policy_Attributes_ListAttributesRequest()
request.namespace = "example.com"
request.pagination.limit = 25
request.pagination.offset = 0
let response = try await client.attributes.listAttributes(request)
print(response)

examples.title: Create an attribute and its values
examples.description: Use the actual namespace ID returned by CreateNamespace. This creates policy objects; associating usable KAS keys and authorizing subjects are separate platform administration tasks.

snippets.code:
from opentdf_tdf3.protocol.policy.attributes import attributes_pb2
from opentdf_tdf3.protocol.policy import objects_pb2

request = attributes_pb2.CreateAttributeRequest(
    namespace_id="11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111",
    name="classification",
    rule=objects_pb2.ATTRIBUTE_RULE_TYPE_ENUM_ANY_OF,
    values=["confidential"],
)
response = await client.attributes.create_attribute_async(request)
print(response)

import OpenTDFTDF3

var request = Policy_Attributes_CreateAttributeRequest()
request.namespaceID = "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111"
request.name = "classification"
request.rule = .anyOf
request.values = ["confidential"]
let response = try await client.attributes.createAttribute(request)
print(response)

examples.title: Look up an attribute by FQN
examples.description: The protobuf JSON request places fqn at the top level. It belongs to the identifier oneof; do not also supply attributeId or the deprecated id field.

snippets.code:
from opentdf_tdf3.protocol.policy.attributes import attributes_pb2

request = attributes_pb2.GetAttributeRequest(
    fqn="https://example.com/attr/classification",
)
response = await client.attributes.get_attribute_async(request)
print(response)

examples.title: Encrypt and decrypt a note
examples.description: Run inside your language's normal function or async entry point. Supply a platform URL, client credentials, and an existing attribute-value FQN from application configuration. Use client credentials only in trusted applications; browser applications should use a token provider. The attribute must have usable KAS mappings and the identity must be entitled to decrypt. The returned archive is binary TDF data. Keep the SDK open and reuse it for subsequent operations.

snippets.code:
import json
from opentdf_tdf3 import SDK

async with await SDK.create_async(
    platform_url, client_id=client_id, client_secret=client_secret,
) as client:
    archive = await client.encrypt_bytes_async(
        b"A confidential note",
        attributes=[attribute_fqn],
        mime_type="text/plain",
        metadata=json.dumps({"name": "note.txt"}),
    )
    plaintext = await client.decrypt_bytes_async(archive)
    print(plaintext.decode("utf-8"))

examples.title: Handle a missing attribute
examples.description: Supply an attribute FQN from your application. Handle only the not_found service code as an absent attribute; preserve other errors, including authentication and permission failures. The C example uses an illustrative fixed FQN and reports other failures to stderr; return or propagate its status according to your application.

examples.title: Authenticate with client credentials
examples.description: Supply a platform URL and credentials from trusted application configuration. Acquire a token through the SDK Auth client to verify authentication, then reuse the SDK for encryption or platform calls. Print the scheme only, not the token value. Run statements in a function or async entry point; Go uses your ctx and C# uses your cancellationToken.

snippets.code:
from opentdf_tdf3 import SDK

async with await SDK.create_async(
    platform_url, client_id=client_id, client_secret=client_secret,
) as client:
    token = await client.auth().access_token_async()
    print("Auth scheme:", token.scheme)

examples.title: Provide an application access token
examples.description: The obtainToken, obtainTokenAsync, obtain_token, ObtainTokenAsync, and provide_access_token functions are application-provided login or refresh operations, not SDK methods. They must observe cancellation and supply a valid Bearer token when called. Go returns (sdk.AccessToken, error); Python returns an awaitable AccessToken; Java and C# return a stage/task of TDF3.AccessToken; Rust returns Result<AccessToken, ProviderError>; Swift implements TokenProvider and completes once. TypeScript obtains {value, expiresAtUnixSeconds} and converts the absolute expiry to bigint. The C callback returns 0 with malloc-owned UTF-8 token JSON in a GXC_BYTES response; keep auth_state valid until the SDK closes. Pass Go callbacks to each operation that needs authentication.

snippets.code:
from opentdf_tdf3 import SDK

async def token_provider(request):
    return await obtain_token(request)

async with await SDK.create_async(
    platform_url, token_provider=token_provider,
) as client:
    token = await client.auth().access_token_async()
    print("Auth scheme:", token.scheme)

examples.title: Use DPoP with client credentials
examples.description: Use a platform and identity provider configured for DPoP and ES256. The SDK creates an ephemeral signing key, obtains a bound token using client credentials, and signs requests. Keep the client alive for subsequent calls. A token supplied by an application provider requires its matching private key and confirmation thumbprint instead; changing the scheme of a Bearer token does not bind it.

snippets.code:
from opentdf_tdf3 import SDK

async with await SDK.create_async(
    platform_url, client_id=client_id, client_secret=client_secret,
    dpop_algorithm="ES256",
) as client:
    token = await client.auth().access_token_async()
    print("Auth scheme:", token.scheme)
